title: Multiplexed imaging and effluent analysis to monitor cancer cell intravasation using a colorectal cancer-on-chip
protocol: Prepare Intestine-chip with appropriate extracellular matrix (ECM).
Activate and apply the ECM to both channels of the chip.
Incubate the chips at 4°C overnight.
Seed HUVECs in the bottom endothelial channel at a density of 6 × 10^6 cells/mL (120,000 cells/chip) in 20 μL/chip.
Invert the chips and incubate at 37°C for 2 h.
Seed Caco2 C2BBe1 cells in the top epithelial channel at a density of 1.25 × 10^6 cells/mL (62,500 cells/chip) in 50 μL/chip.
Incubate at 37°C for 2 h.
Remove any apparent bubbles within the chip.
Connect chips to pods and initiate a regulate cycle.
Harvest HCT116 H2B-GFP cells from a 10 cm plate by washing with 1× DPBS, adding 2–3 ml of 0.05% Trypsin-EDTA, and incubating at 37°C for 5 min.
Collect detached cells using a P1000 and place in a 15 mL Falcon tube.
Add Complete DMEM Cell Culture Media to the 15 mL Falcon tube containing HCT116 H2B-GFP cell suspension to bring the total volume to 15 ml.
Warm Complete DMEM Cell Culture Media for 1 hour prior to use.
Centrifuge the cells at 200 × g for 5 minutes at room temperature (20°C–22°C).
Discard the supernatant and resuspend the cells in a small volume of Complete DMEM Cell Culture Media.
Count cells using an automated cell counter.
Prepare a cell suspension of 400,000 cells/mL in 50 μL/chip.
Remove the pods from the Zoë and place them in the biosafety cabinet (BSC).
Disconnect chips from pods.
Seed 35–50 μL of the HCT116 H2B-GFP cell suspension into the top epithelial channel of one chip.
Check the seeding density and distribution of the cells under a microscope to ensure even cell seeding across the length of the channel.
Incubate for 2 hours at 37°C.
Re-prime pods as described by Emulate.
Reconnect chips to pods, ensuring a liquid-liquid interface to prevent bubble formation.
Resume fluid flow after reconnection.
Initiate a regulate cycle upon reconnection if necessary to ensure proper fluid flow.
Maintain chips for 7 days.
Replenish media every 3 days.
Aspirate outflows to prevent pod overflow.
Warm specific media at 37°C for 1 hour prior to addition to pod reservoirs.
Maintain chips for 7 days or up to 14 days as needed by the user.
Initiate cyclic stretching after D0 imaging is completed using Zoë instruments set to 10% deformation at 0.2 Hz.
Collect effluent media from pod reservoirs.
Centrifuge collected media.
Transfer supernatant into appropriately labeled microcentrifuge tubes for downstream analysis.
Resuspend and plate any cells found in the endothelial effuent for counting or further characterization.
Aspirate bottom and top channel outflow reservoirs 2 days prior to desired date of media collection.
Collect 100–200 μL inlet media from the top and bottom pod inlet reservoirs of all chips of the same condition.
Place collected inlet media into appropriately labeled 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tubes.
Combine channel specific inlet media across multiple chips if necessary to collect the desired 1 mL media.
Collect 1 mL outlet media from the top and bottom pod outlet reservoirs of each chip.
Place collected outlet media into appropriately labeled 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tubes for effluent media collection and cell resuspension.
Centrifuge the microcentrifuge tubes at 200 × g for 5 min.
Collect the supernatant and place it into a freshly labeled 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tube.
Leave about 100 μL of supernatant in each tube for cell resuspension.
Ensure not to disrupt any visible or non-visible pellet while collecting the supernatant.
Freeze the collected supernatant and store at −80°C for future use in mass spectrometry and similar assays.
Resuspend any cells present in the microcentrifuge tube with the remaining 100 μL.
Plate the resuspended cells onto a 96-well plate.
Incubate the plate at 37°C until cells have settled and adhered to the plate (roughly 2–3 h).
Image the 96-well plate utilizing the Operetta High Content Screening platform at a wavelength of 488 nm to capture HCT116 H2B-GFP cells.
Input images into Perkin Elmer Harmony image analysis software for segmentation and counting of GFP+ cells.
Collect effluent media prior to imaging to minimize disconnection time for chips from flow.
Image chips approximately 12–16 hours after HCT116 seeding (D0).
Transfer pods from the Zoës to the BSC before imaging.
Detach one chip at a time from its pod and place it on the stage of the Olympus FV3000 laser scanning confocal microscope for imaging.
Image 6 regions across the span of the chip where the top and bottom channels overlap (excluding top and bottom inlet and outlet regions).
Image six regions of the CRC-on-chip via confocal microscopy.
Identify the number of GFP+ cells in each channel using image analysis software.
Produce an invasion ratio by comparing the number of GFP+ cells in the bottom channel relative to the top channel at each time point.
Normalize invasion ratios to D0 counts.
Image HCT116 H2B-GFP cells with the 488 nm laser.
Image RFP-HUVECs with the 561 nm laser.
Use transmitted light microscopy for identification of unlabeled Caco2 C2BBe1 cells in the epithelial channel.
Image from the bottom layer of the endothelial channel up through the epithelial channel (about 400 μm Z-height) at 5 μm intervals.
Return chip to the BSC after imaging.
Reconnect chip to pod and resume normal fluid flow.
Ensure there is a liquid-liquid interface between the chip and the pod.
Re-prime the pods as necessary per Emulate’s protocols.
Input images into Imaris imaging software.
Use the Imaris cell detection algorithm ("spot detection" function) to find the number of GFP+ cells in each region.
Set the spot detection algorithm to identify cells with a xy diameter of 8 μm and include background subtraction.
Record the number of GFP+ tumor cells and calculate invasion ratio for each time point.
